source_text: Videturne assertor locuples iudiciorum suorum Deus, qui tam multis capitibus de hac quaestione non solum iudicavit, sed etiam disputavit? Plane, qui temporum nostrorum praevideret errores, tanta verborum suorum vel luce vel copia duo est iuste operatus et provide: unum, ne quis ulla quaestionum ambiguitate moveretur, aliud, ne apud eos, qui se immersissent sponte naufragiis, excusationis tabula ulla remaneret. Loquitur ad Iudaeos, qui captivitatem sceleribus exigentes ad revelandam propriae praevaricationis invidiam parentibus, non moribus suis debitam eam fuisse iactabant, et convenit eos auctoritate patria: Utquid vobis, inquit, istam parabolam, ut dicatis: Parentes manducaverunt uvas acerbas et filiorum dentes obstupuerunt? Vivo ego, dicit Adonai Dominus, si dicetur amplius parabola haec in Israel, quoniam omnes animae meae sunt, quemadmodum anima patris, ita anima filii; omnes animae meae sunt. Anima, quae peccat, ipsa morietur [n50] .
pass_a_gloss: Does God seem a wealthy asserter of his own judgments, who in so many heads has not only judged concerning this question but even disputed? Plainly, he who would foresee the errors of our times has by so great a light or abundance of his words justly and providently worked two things: one, that no one be moved by any ambiguity of questions; another, that among those who had immersed themselves willingly in shipwrecks no plank of excuse remain. He speaks to the Jews, who, exacting captivity by crimes, to reveal the envy of their own transgression were boasting that it had been owed to parents, not to their own manners, and he convenes them with paternal authority: Why to you, he says, this parable, that you say: Parents have eaten sour grapes and the teeth of the sons have been set on edge? I live, says Adonai the Lord, if this parable shall still be said in Israel, since all souls are mine, as the soul of the father, so the soul of the son; all souls are mine. The soul which sins, itself will die.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Does God not appear a fully competent defender of his own judgments, when on this question he has not only passed judgment but also reasoned through so many points? Clearly, foreseeing the errors of our times, he justly and providently accomplished two things through the brightness and abundance of his words. First, no one should be unsettled by any ambiguity in the questions. Second, those who willingly plunged into shipwreck should have no plank of excuse remaining.

He speaks to the Jews, whose crimes had earned captivity. To divert the blame for their own disobedience, they claimed captivity was owed to their parents rather than to their own conduct. He confronts them with a father’s authority: ‘Why do you use this proverb: The parents ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge? As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be spoken in Israel. All souls are mine: the father’s soul and the son’s soul alike—all souls are mine. The soul that sins shall itself die’ (Ezekiel 18:2–4).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
